neet_che_u11_t04_1.working: In the final step, Na2Cr2O7 + 2KCl → K2Cr2O7 + 2NaCl. K2Cr2O7 is less soluble, so it crystallises out as orange crystals.

neet_che_u11_t04_2.working: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, MnO4- is reduced to MnO2. Iodide is oxidised to iodate: 2MnO4- + H2O + I- → 2MnO2 + 2OH- + IO3-.

neet_che_u11_t04_3.working: The dichromate ion consists of two CrO4 tetrahedra sharing one corner oxygen. The Cr–O–Cr bond is bent, at about 126°.

neet_che_u11_t04_4.working: K2Cr2O7 can be weighed accurately because it is non-hygroscopic, available pure and stable. This makes it suitable as a primary standard, so R explains A.

neet_che_u11_t04_5.working: Statement I: 4FeCr2O4 + 8Na2CO3 + 7O2 → 8Na2CrO4 + 2Fe2O3 + 8CO2, so it is correct. Statement II: 3MnO4^2- + 4H+ → 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O gives 2 mol MnO4- and 1 mol MnO2, so the statement has them reversed and is incorrect.
